correctness.rationale: The source gives an iff regular expression for one-run starts and an exhaustive finite set of zero-run lengths. Parameterizing the regular expression yields four length families, with \(\binom{t+2}{2}\) representations at parameter sum \(t\); summation gives the exact binomial formula and leading coefficient \(1/12\). At a Fibonacci cutoff, representation length converts directly to numeric size. Each one-run has a distinct preceding zero-run, while every zero-run has length at most 13, giving the two-sided sandwich. Fibonacci exponential growth then converts cubic representation-length growth to \(\Theta((\log N)^3)\). The verifier independently checks the combinatorial count and direct finite cube endings.

value.rationale: The primary paper motivates cube-ending frequency as a measure of how close the Fibonacci word is to periodic and proves only that exceptions have density zero. The new theorem supplies the first sharp scale for that deficit—cubic in logarithmic length—plus an exact count of run starts at natural Fibonacci cutoffs. This is a structural quantitative refinement of the paper's central measure, not an arbitrary finite slice.
